tagline: The world's most expensive homes, nano flats, and everyone's favourite topic.
why: Property is Hong Kong's national obsession. Homes are among the most expensive on earth relative to income, so buying, renting, mortgages and prices come up at every family dinner. After years of falling prices since 2021, the market has been trying to find a bottom. Knowing the vocabulary, the big developers and the policy changes makes you fluent in the city's favourite small talk.

essentials.title: Extremely expensive
essentials.body: Hong Kong has topped global unaffordability rankings for years, with home prices many times the median household income.

essentials.title: Prices fell after 2021
essentials.body: Prices peaked in 2021, then dropped around 25-30% amid rising rates, emigration and weak demand. By 2025 the market showed signs of stabilising.

essentials.title: Saleable area is what matters
essentials.body: Flats are measured in square feet, and since 2013 prices must be quoted by saleable area (actual usable space), not the inflated gross area.

essentials.title: Public vs private housing
essentials.body: About half the population lives in public rental housing or subsidised Home Ownership Scheme (HOS) flats. Waiting times for public housing are years long.

essentials.title: Policy moves the market
essentials.body: The government removed all the 'spicy' extra stamp duties in February 2024 and has loosened mortgage rules to support prices.

essentials.title: Rates drive affordability
essentials.body: Mortgages are tied to HIBOR or the prime rate, which follow US rates. Rate cuts make buying cheaper.

essentials.title: Developers are powerful
essentials.body: A handful of tycoon-led developers built much of Hong Kong and hold huge land banks.

now.headline: Prices up about 7% this year
now.detail: Official data show private home prices rose 0.19% in September, up 7.1% for the first nine months and 9.3% on a year ago.

now.headline: Rents at a record
now.detail: The official rent index hit a new high in September, up 6.2% year on year; small flats yield about 3.5%.

now.headline: Resale prices cooling
now.detail: Centaline's CCL slipped to about 160 in mid-October as developers launched new projects at aggressive prices.

now.headline: New-home rush
now.detail: Developers sold about 1,700 new flats in the first 27 days of October, the third straight month above 1,000.

now.headline: Rate-hike worry
now.detail: With the US Fed expected to hike in December, buyers watch HIBOR; most banks cap effective mortgage rates at 3.25%.

local.headline: Small talk staple
local.detail: 'Are you renting or buying?' and 'which district?' are standard conversation.

local.headline: Living with parents
local.detail: Many adults live with parents into their thirties because of prices.

local.headline: Car parks cost millions
local.detail: Parking spaces regularly sell for several million dollars.

local.headline: Feng shui
local.detail: Unlucky numbers like 4 are skipped in buildings, and flats with 'bad' history sell at discounts.

debates.question: Buy or rent?
debates.sides: Buying builds equity and stability; renting stays flexible while prices are uncertain.

debates.question: Is there enough land?
debates.sides: Some say release land and country park edges; others say protect green space and use brownfield sites.

debates.question: Will prices recover?
debates.sides: Optimists cite rate cuts and new arrivals; pessimists cite oversupply and emigration.

debates.question: Are nano flats acceptable?
debates.sides: Affordable entry vs inhumane living sizes.
